newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY - SENATORS REACH MODEST HOME VICTORY MILESTONE.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY - SENATORS REACH MODEST HOME VICTORY MILESTONE.

text.p: Shaun Van Allen scored twice in a three-goal first period as the Ottawa Senators reached 10 home victories for the first time in their five-year history with a 6-4 win over the Vancouver Canucks on Monday.
Alexei Yashin had a goal -- his 24th -- and two assists, Steve Duchesne had a goal and an assist and Janne Laukkanen and Randy Cunneyworth set up two goals apiece for Ottawa.
"I really have been enjoying playing lately," said Yashin, "but I don't think it's just me, it's a team game and a line game and we're just all playing well right now."
The Senators improved to 5-2-3 in their last 10 games and raised their record at home to 10-14-6.

Ottawa built a commanding 5-1 lead and took a 5-2 advantage into the third period. But David Roberts and Mike Ridley scored less than three minutes apart for Vancouver in the third period to make it a one-goal game.

The Canucks put on heavy pressure in the Ottawa zone in an attempt to knot the score. But Senators winger Denny Lambert made a perfect breakout pass to Alexandre Daigle, who converted the breakaway for his 20th goal with 78 seconds left to seal the victory.
"This is one of the most improved teams in the NHL," Vancouver coach Tom Renney said of the Senators.
In Calgary, Stephane Fiset made 38 saves, including 14 in the third period, and the Kings came up with three special teams goals in the second period as Los Angeles edged the Flames 3-2.
Yanic Perreault had a short-handed goal and Ed Olczyk and Kai Nurminen scored on the power play for the Kings, who had just one goal in their previous three meetings with Calgary.
Steve Chiasson scored in the final minute of the second for Calgary and Theo Fleury's 22nd goal 7:54 into the third pulled the Flames within one. But Fiset shut down Calgary the rest of the way.
In Montreal, Johan Garpenlov's wrist shot beat goaltender Jose Theodore with 3:30 left in regulation to lift the Florida Panthers into a 2-2 tie with the Canadiens.
Garpenlov's scored through a screen, spoiling a superb performance by Theodore, who made 39 saves after stepping in at the last minute for Jocelyn Thibault who sat out with the flu.
Martin Rucinsky and Vladimir Malakhov scored for the Canadiens, while Scott Mellanby had the other goal for Florida. All three were powerplay tallies.
In San Jose, Ulf Dahlen's third goal in as many games snapped a first-period tie and the Chicago Blackhawks skated to a 4-2 victory over the Sharks.

Tony Amonte's shot was stopped by San Jose goaltender Kelly Hrudey, but Dahlen poked in the rebound from behind the net with 77 seconds left in the first period to give Chicago a 2-1 lead over his former team.
Bob Probert and Eric Daze added insurance goals for the Blackhawks, who got 38 saves from Chris Terreri.
Terreri, Dahlen and Michal Sykora were traded to Chicago for goaltender Ed Belfour on January 25. Belfour was sidelined by a knee strain.
